_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the Minetest egg in https://github.com/pterodactyl/game-eggs (MIT).
name: Luanti
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: The open source voxel game engine, formerly Minetest. Builds the chosen Luanti release's server and downloads the chosen game from ContentDB, for x86-64 and ARM nodes; worlds, mods, games and minetest.conf are kept.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Luanti (formerly Minetest): builds the chosen Luanti release's server from
# its source (Luanti publishes no Linux server binaries), and downloads the
# chosen game from ContentDB, checked against ContentDB's SHA-256, when it
# isn't there yet. Worlds, mods, games and minetest.conf are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=luanti-org/luanti
ua="raptor-egg-library/1.0 (+https://raptorpanel.net)"
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT

want="${LUANTI_VERSION:-latest}"
tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$want" 2>/dev/null) ||
    fail "Luanti has no release $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $(gh-release tag "$repo" latest 2>/dev/null || echo 5.18.0)."

if [ "$(cat .raptor-luanti 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag $(uname -m)" ] && [ -x bin/luantiserver ]; then
    echo "Luanti $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Building the Luanti $tag server, which takes a few minutes"
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    { apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends g++ make cmake \
        libsqlite3-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev zlib1g-dev libzstd-dev libluajit-5.1-dev; } >/dev/null ||
        fail "The build tools couldn't be installed. Reinstall to try again."
    rm -rf "$build"; mkdir -p "$build"
    git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$tag" "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$build/src" ||
        fail "Luanti's source can't be downloaded right now. Reinstall to try again."
    tri=$(gcc -dumpmachine)
    # LuaJIT, JsonCpp and GMP built in, so the server runs on the plain runtime image.
    cmake -S "$build/src" -B "$build/out" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DRUN_IN_PLACE=TRUE \
        -DBUILD_CLIENT=FALSE -DBUILD_SERVER=TRUE -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=FALSE -DENABLE_GETTEXT=FALSE \
        -DENABLE_CURSES=FALSE -DENABLE_PROMETHEUS=FALSE -DENABLE_SPATIAL=FALSE -DENABLE_REDIS=FALSE \
        -DENABLE_POSTGRESQL=FALSE -DENABLE_LEVELDB=FALSE -DENABLE_SYSTEM_JSONCPP=FALSE -DENABLE_SYSTEM_GMP=FALSE \
        -DLUA_LIBRARY="/usr/lib/$tri/libluajit-5.1.a" -DLUA_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/include/luajit-2.1 >"$build/cmake.log" ||
        { tail -n 20 "$build/cmake.log"; fail "Luanti $tag couldn't be configured to build."; }
    # One compiler per ~700 MB of the install's memory (at least 1 GB, the
    # server's if more), so a small server doesn't run out mid-build.
    jobs=$(( ${SERVER_MEMORY:-1024} / 700 )); [ "$jobs" -ge 1 ] || jobs=1
    [ "$jobs" -le "$(nproc)" ] || jobs=$(nproc)
    make -C "$build/out" -j"$jobs" >"$build/make.log" 2>&1 ||
        { tail -n 30 "$build/make.log"; fail "Luanti $tag didn't build. If the log above says Killed, give the server more memory, then reinstall."; }
    server=$(ls "$build/src/bin/luantiserver" "$build/src/bin/minetestserver" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
    [ -n "$server" ] || fail "Luanti $tag built no server."
    mkdir -p bin
    cp -f "$server" bin/luantiserver.new && mv -f bin/luantiserver.new bin/luantiserver
    # The engine's own Lua code, replaced to match the new server.
    rm -rf builtin.new && cp -a "$build/src/builtin" builtin.new && rm -rf builtin && mv builtin.new builtin
    cp -f "$build/src/minetest.conf.example" . 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "$tag $(uname -m)" > .raptor-luanti
fi

mkdir -p games mods worlds
game="${CONTENTDB_GAME:-}"
if [ -n "$game" ]; then
    name=${game#*/}
    if [ -d "games/$name" ]; then
        echo "The game $name is already in games."
    else
        rel=$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" "https://content.luanti.org/api/packages/$game/releases/") ||
            fail "ContentDB has no package $game. Set Game to a game's author/name from content.luanti.org, such as Luanti/minetest_game."
        url=$(jq -r '.[0].url // empty' <<<"$rel"); sum=$(jq -r '.[0].sha256 // empty' <<<"$rel")
        [ -n "$url" ] || fail "ContentDB's package $game has no release to download."
        echo "Downloading $game from ContentDB"
        mkdir -p "$build/game"
        curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" -o "$build/game.zip" "$url"
        [ -z "$sum" ] || [ "$(sha256sum "$build/game.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] || fail "The download of $game didn't match ContentDB's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
        unzip -q "$build/game.zip" -d "$build/game"
        conf=$(find "$build/game" -maxdepth 2 -name game.conf | head -n1)
        [ -n "$conf" ] || fail "$game isn't a game: it has no game.conf. Set Game to a game, not a mod."
        mv "$(dirname "$conf")" "games/$name"
    fi
fi

if [ ! -f minetest.conf ]; then
    cat > minetest.conf <<'CONF'
# Luanti's settings: minetest.conf.example lists them all.
server_name = Luanti server
server_description = A Luanti server
server_announce = false
max_users = 15
name = admin
default_password =
motd =
CONF
fi
echo "Installed Luanti $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Luanti release to build, such as 5.18.0, or latest. Players need this version or newer.

variables.name: Game
variables.description: A game from content.luanti.org to download at install, as author/name. Empty downloads none: upload one to games instead.

variables.name: Game ID
variables.description: The game a new world uses: its folder name in games.

variables.name: World name
variables.description: The world's folder in worlds. A new world is made when there's none by this name.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: The name shown in the server list.

variables.name: Description
variables.description: The description shown in the server list.

variables.name: Show in server list
variables.description: true lists the server on the public server list.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: The most players that can be connected at once.

variables.name: Admin name
variables.description: The player who gets every privilege when they join with this name.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: The password new players need to join. Empty lets anyone join.

variables.name: Message of the day
variables.description: The message players see when they join.
